inconsistencies: Rebroadcast privacy is attacked by six overlapping PRs: #36398 (only rebroadcast IsFromMe), #36482 (only announce what was re-added to mempool), #36330 (no resubmission under -privatebroadcast), #34533 (resubmit via private broadcast instead), #36380 (-walletbroadcast=initialonly) and #36481 (manual rebroadcast). Review #36398 first since it sets the baseline policy the others build on.

#34533 and #36330 are opposite approaches to the identical defect (wallet resubmission defeating -privatebroadcast); they were previously split P1/P2. They now share P2 and a decision on approach should precede review of either.
Dependency chain #33033 (SQLite RAII) -> #33034 (tx table) -> #27865 (no-longer-spendable TXOs): review base-first; #33033 was scored P3 but cannot sit below the P2 work it unblocks.
Dependency chain #36442 -> #36443 -> #36444 (multipath descriptors): #36443 was scored P3 but is a prerequisite for P2 #36444, so it was raised and the three are kept contiguous.
#35302 (Silent Payments sending) is stated to help unblock #32966 (receiving); review sending first despite receiving scoring higher alone.
#10102 (multiprocess) is the base for #19460; #19460 cannot be evaluated independently of it.
#35918, #36070 and #36143 are all prerequisites for the same multisig wizard project (#35645) and should be reviewed as one block rather than in isolation.
#35492 (fail dump on incomplete writes) and #35998 (handle WalletBatch write failures) address the same class of defect — ignored persistence failures; #35998 is the systemic fix and should go first.

#34193 (migration robustness) and #34909 (move ~800 lines of migration code out of wallet.cpp) touch the same code; the behavior fix #34193 should land before the move-only refactor. #36333 also touches migration-time transaction deletion.
#35716 (multi_index for mapWallet) overlaps the transaction-storage rework in #33034/#27865; coordinate so one does not invalidate the other.

#36488 (deprecate confTarget) and #36489 (add snake_case funding aliases) are the same RPC option-naming cleanup from the same author and should be reviewed together; #36489 also carries an actual bug fix.
#36550 supersedes #36551 per its own description; only one should be reviewed.
result.notes: This is an unusually large category and the P2 band is correspondingly wide: it holds the migration/storage correctness fixes, the PSBT and hardware-signer interoperability fixes, the rebroadcast-privacy cluster, and the two multi-PR feature projects (Silent Payments, multipath descriptors). P1 was reserved for defects that can lose funds, corrupt or destroy wallet data, crash loading, silently hide balances, or leak node identity for all wallet users. Several bands were adjusted only to keep dependency chains from inverting (#33033, #36443) or to put PRs attacking the identical defect in the same band (#34533 vs #36330).
